# Problem

All 10 planning/analysis/maintenance skills use placeholder `--ac` values in their final-step `render_report` blocks. Agents therefore pass the work item's feature ACs (unmet pre-implementation), causing the report to show "incomplete" when the skill session actually completed.

SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5 made `render_report()` derive session status from AC verdicts: any unmet → "incomplete". SA-0MUUCNXNG004RG5Z fixed intake by passing concrete process-deliverable ACs. This child fixes the remaining 10 skills.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each SKILL.md's final-step `--ac` block replaced with concrete skill-session deliverable ACs (4 per skill for skills with multiple deliverables; 3 for simpler skills).
2. Each final-step block includes a one-line note: "> **Note:** ACs record the *skill session's* own deliverables — not the work item's feature acceptance criteria."
3. No code changes — SKILL.md docs only.
4. Full test suite green (existing tests unaffected by doc-only changes).
5. No new `--ac` lines change the renderer's behaviour; all `--ac` values use the "met" verdict on success.

## Skills affected

- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: plan approved, children created, ACs traceable.
- `skill/find-related/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: keyword derivation, wl search, repo file search, summary compiled.
- `skill/effort-and-risk/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: PERT estimate computed, risk score assessed, confidence stated, WBS suggested.
- `skill/triage/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: test failures parsed, critical items triaged, work items created/linked.
- `skill/author-command/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: command spec drafted, SKILL.md written, script stub created, tests written.
- `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: branches assessed, stale branches pruned, orphaned stashes triaged, comments posted.
- `skill/code-review/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: code quality analysis run, findings documented, recommendations provided.
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: code smells detected, refactoring plan drafted, changes applied.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: machine pressure assessed, safe remediations proposed, actions logged.
- `skill/resolve-pr-comments/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: PR comments fetched, fixes proposed, threads resolved after approval.

## Risks

- Adding `--ac` lines to each SKILL.md is a mechanical but widespread change. Mitigation: each change is independent and reversible.
- If a skill's final-step block is very long, adding ACs + note might make it verbose. Mitigation: ACs are concise (40–60 chars each).

## Related

- **SA-0MUUI6ZCX001RO8V** — Epic (parent).
- **SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5** — Renderer conditional header/conclusion.
- **SA-0MUUCNXNG004RG5Z** — Intake SKILL.md fix (sibling, in_review).
- **SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR** — Adds "Use Cases" section for work-item ACs.
data.title: Add concrete skill-session ACs to planning/analysis/maintenance skills

# Problem

The 4 operational/delivery skills (test, ship, implement, audit) use placeholder `--ac` values. For test/ship the session ACs are the operational deliverables (suite run, failures triaged / release promoted, audit performed). For implement/audit, the semantics are different — these skills evaluate the work item's ACs as part of their session, which is a legitimate use of `--ac`. This child clarifies the distinction and aligns with SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **test** (`skill/test/SKILL.md`): `--ac` block replaced with 4 skill-session ACs: full test suite executed, failures parsed into triage records, critical failures triaged into work items, report rendered.
2. **ship** (`skill/ship/SKILL.md`): `--ac` block replaced with 4 skill-session ACs: dev-to-main merge performed, audit comment posted, operator notified, CHANGELOG updated.
3. **implement** (`skill/implement/SKILL.md`): `--ac` block updated with skill-session ACs: worktree created, tests written/updated, build green, tests green, commit made, push to dev. **Note added:** "For implement, the work-item feature ACs are evaluated during execution but are not passed to `render_report` — the report records the implement session's own success criteria. Work-item ACs are displayed in the Use Cases section (SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR)."
4. **audit** (`skill/audit/SKILL.md`): `--ac` block updated with skill-session ACs: work item assessed, audit verdict determined, Ready to close line added. **Note added:** "For audit, the verdict reflects the work item's state; the report records the audit session's own success criteria (audit was performed). Work-item ACs are displayed in the Use Cases section (SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR)."
5. No code changes — SKILL.md docs only.
6. Full test suite green.

## Skills affected

- `skill/test/SKILL.md`
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md`
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md`
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`

## Risks

- **Implement/audit semantics**: these skills legitimately evaluate work-item ACs. The note clarifies that the report's `--ac` table still records session success (not work-item status), and work-item ACs go in the Use Cases section.
- If SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR ("Use Cases" section) is not yet implemented, the notes reference it as a dependency.

## Related

- **SA-0MUUI6ZCX001RO8V** — Epic (parent).
- **SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5** — Renderer conditional header/conclusion.
- **SA-0MUUCNXNG004RG5Z** — Intake SKILL.md fix (sibling).
- **SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR** — Adds "Use Cases" section for work-item ACs.

# Problem

There is no automated guard against future regressions of the placeholder-`--ac` pattern. Agents adding new report-rendering skills (or editing existing ones) might again use `--ac "<AC# description>|…|met"` placeholders instead of concrete skill-session deliverables.

SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S already added `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` which checks that every work-item skill has the final-step section and invokes `render_report`. This child extends it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Extend `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` with a new test class `TestReportACConcreteness`:
   - `test_all_final_step_acs_are_concrete`: asserts each work-item skill's `--ac` lines contain at least one literal `|met` value (no placeholders like `<AC# description>`).
   - `test_all_final_steps_have_semantics_note`: asserts each work-item skill's final-step block contains a note distinguishing skill-session ACs from work-item feature ACs (search for patterns like "skill session" or "own deliverable" in the final-step block).
2. Add the new test class to the existing test file (no new test files).
3. All 6 existing hygiene tests still pass.
4. Full test suite green.

## Tests

- `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` — extended with `TestReportACConcreteness` (2 new tests).

## Skills covered

The test covers all 15 skills in `WORK_ITEM_SKILLS` (audit, author-command, cleanup, code-review, effort-and-risk, find-related, implement, intake, machine-hygiene, plan, refactor, resolve-pr-comments, ship, test, triage).

## Related

- **SA-0MUUI6ZCX001RO8V** — Epic (parent).
- **SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S** — Original report helper work (existing hygiene test).

# Migrate implement.py repo/worktree fixtures to git_sandbox

Parent: SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0

## Goal

Route every real-git invocation in the `implement.py` test fixtures through
`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` so a leaked repository-overriding environment
cannot redirect the fixture away from its `tmp_path` sandbox.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fixtures in `tests/test_implement_worktree_repo_root.py`,
  `tests/test_implement_submodules.py`,
  `tests/test_implement_node_modules_symlink.py`,
  `tests/test_implement_abort_safety.py` and
  `tests/test_implement_code_freeze_gate.py` use `gs.init_repo`,
  `gs.commit_all`, `gs.add_worktree` and `gs.run_git`; no bare
  `subprocess.run(["git", …])` remains in these files.
- [ ] Each migrated fixture helper has a behavioural regression test proving a
  leaked `GIT_DIR` cannot redirect it (victim repo unchanged; the fixture repo
  resolves under `tmp_path`), mirroring
  `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py::TestEnvironmentIsolation` and
  `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py::TestRepoHelpersAreHermetic`.
- [ ] Every `implement.py` subprocess runner in these files passes
  `gs.sanitized_git_env()` so a leaked override cannot reach the child's git
  invocations (as already done in
  `tests/test_implement_worktree_enforcement.py::_run_violation_check`).
- [ ] `default_branch` is set correctly so fixtures that relied on a `dev`
  branch (e.g. `git branch dev` after init) do not create a spurious or
  duplicate branch.
- [ ] Fixture identity is injected via the sandbox (`-c user.name=… -c user.email=…`) rather than relying on a repo-local `git config` in the helper; any remaining identity `config` in a migrated helper is explicit and deliberate.
- [ ] All existing behavioural assertions in the five files pass unchanged.

## Minimal Implementation

- Replace each fixture's `git init` + `config user.*` + `add` + `commit` +
  `branch dev` sequence with `gs.init_repo(..., default_branch="dev")` +
  `gs.commit_all(...)`; replace `git worktree add` with `gs.add_worktree(...)`.
- Keep subprocess-runner helper scripts, but spawn them with
  `env=gs.sanitized_git_env()`.
- Add one hermetic regression test per migrated fixture (victim + leaked
  `GIT_DIR`).

## Key Files

- `tests/test_implement_worktree_repo_root.py`
- `tests/test_implement_submodules.py`
- `tests/test_implement_node_modules_symlink.py`
- `tests/test_implement_abort_safety.py`
- `tests/test_implement_code_freeze_gate.py`

## Dependencies

F1 (tracer-bullet recipe and regression template).

# Full-suite verification, docs and final bare-git sweep

Parent: SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0

## Goal

Close out the migration: prove the repo is free of the non-hermetic pattern
(within the documented exclusions), that the full suite is green, and that the
documentation reflects the final state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The full project suite passes via `/skill:test` (`run_tests.py --scope
  full`) with the migrated helpers in place; any failures are triaged through
  the triage skill.
- [ ] A repo-wide AST sweep confirms no test helper under `tests/` or
  `skill/**/tests/` invokes `git` via a bare `subprocess.run(["git", …])`, with
  the documented exclusions (`tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py` embedded
  string-literal mutation proofs, which must not be routed through the
  sandbox).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and any `docs/dev/` entries such as `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`.
- [ ] `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` documents the final migrated state
  (including `skill/shared/validate_fanout.py`'s env-only treatment), and
  `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` anti-pattern #7 is updated only if
  the migration revealed a gap.
- [ ] No test depends on ambient git identity or a leaked environment (fixture
  identity is injected via the sandbox).
- [ ] Findings that are out of scope (e.g. new test-quality issues) are
  recorded as linked work items rather than folded into this item.

## Minimal Implementation

- Run `/skill:test` at full scope; triage failures.
- Re-run the AST sweep and record the result as a work-item comment.
- Update the docs to match the final state.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`

F1, F2, F3, F4, F5 (all migrations must land first).

Discovered-from:SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS.

## Goal

Prevent recurrence of the author-identity-gate refusal by adding `pi@local` to `syncAllowedAuthors` in `.worklog/config.yaml` (project scope), so future pi-session-authored worklog sync commits pass the gate.

## Background

Operator decision (2026-10-16, SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS Decisions+Appendix): add `pi@local` to the allow list for this project. Intentional consequence: the project gate accepts `pi@local` authors; the empty-email gate is never bypassed; arbitrary foreign emails remain refused. The general guard `scripts/check_git_identity.py` must NOT be hardened to flag `pi@local` (that would contradict this allow-list).

**Why this is the durable fix:** the 4 offending commits and 3 older `pi@local` commits (7 total) remain in the shared `refs/worklog/data` history. A fresh clone has no `last-synced-ref`, so the gate scans the entire remote ref history and would refuse again until this allow-list entry lands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** `pi@local` is added to `syncAllowedAuthors` in `.worklog/config.yaml` (project scope), with a comment explaining the deliberate widening and referencing SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS.
- [ ] **AC2** The regression test child (`Author-gate allow-list regression tests`) is green and its red-before/green-after evidence is recorded.
- [ ] **AC3** `check_git_identity.py` is unchanged (no new hardening flagging `pi@local`); its existing test suite stays green.

## Key Files

- `.worklog/config.yaml`

## Dependencies

- Blocked-by: SA-0MVBD5MXS007WJT0 (Author-gate allow-list regression tests — TDD contract first).

## Deliverables

- Updated `.worklog/config.yaml` + passing tests + commit comment.

Child of SA-0MVE995PV0077QB5 (Raise TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY 2->3 with mini-F7 validation). Core code change, gated by the measurement.

## Goal

As an agent session, I want the host-wide test-suite ceiling raised from 2 to 3 once it is measured as safe, so a third suite starts instead of waiting up to `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (600 s) while CPUs sit idle.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT` is `3` in `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`.
- The module docstring (~line 24), the constant's comment (~line 139) and `_test_semaphore_max_workers()`'s docstring (~line 1308) all state the value `3` and cite SA-0MVE995PV0077QB5 plus the calibration artifact `docs/dev/test-ceiling-validation.json`.
- Precedence (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` env > default) is unchanged; values below 1 still clamp to 1 and invalid values still warn and fall back to the default.
- Semantics are untouched: bounded wait, `TEST_LOCK_JITTER` staggering, cache hits never acquiring a slot, the separate `audit`/`audit-host` namespaces and nested-run isolation all behave exactly as before (no behavioural diff beyond the ceiling number).
- The tests from SA-0MVE995PV0077QB5.3 pass (previously red, now green) and the existing 17 semaphore tests still pass.
- No other default in the file changes (e.g. `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `TEST_LOCK_JITTER` untouched).
- The change is committed with the changed-scope test gate green (build -> test -> commit order).

- Parent AC1 traceability: default raised and documented in code — `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT` is `3` in `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`; the module docstring, constant comment and `_test_semaphore_max_workers()` docstring state the value and cite this work item, and precedence/clamping are unchanged.
## Minimal implementation

- One-line constant change plus three documentation touch-ups (module docstring, constant comment, resolver docstring).
- Cite the measured numbers briefly in the constant comment (e.g. "calibrated 2026-xx: 8-suite drain at 3 <= 1.10x ceiling 2, load delta < 4, no swap growth").
- No restructuring, no new constants, no dynamic CPU-count sizing (out of scope).

## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`
- `skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_semaphore.py` (must go green)
- `docs/dev/test-ceiling-validation.json` (cited evidence)

## Dependencies

- SA-0MVE995PV0077QB5.3 (default-pinning tests, test-first).
- SA-0MVE995PV0077QB5.2 measurement must have PASSED its gate.

## Deliverables

- Default raised to 3 with documented rationale in code.

Child of SA-0MVE995PV0077QB5 (Raise TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY 2->3 with mini-F7 validation).

## Goal

As an operator reading the docs, I want every statement of the test concurrency default and the nested-run deadlock example to match reality, so I do not size environments or debug deadlocks against a stale ceiling.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` env table shows `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` default `3`.
- The nested-run deadlock example (section 0.6) is rewritten from "two concurrent full suites ... `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2`" to the ceiling-3 equivalent (three concurrent full suites), **without** weakening the isolation contract.
- A short calibration subsection in `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` links `docs/dev/test-ceiling-validation.json`, states the measured pass gate (load delta < 4, no swap growth, drain <= 1.10x), and names the blocker that made the raise safe.
- `docs/dev/fanout-validation-report.md` gains a section (or a new companion section) documenting the test-ceiling run: method, results table, conclusion.
- A repo-wide search for the old default finds no remaining stale statement (`grep -rn "TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY" docs/ skill/ README.md` reviewed); each remaining occurrence is either correct or updated.
- `CHANGELOG.md` is not edited (managed by the ship skill's release pipeline).

- Parent AC4 traceability: documentation updated — `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` (env table `2` -> `3`, the nested-run deadlock example, and a calibration subsection linking the measurement) and `docs/dev/fanout-validation-report.md` (a section documenting this run).
- Parent AC7 traceability: all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries — non-existent surfaces are checked and the result recorded.
## Minimal implementation

- Update the env table row and both stale references (lines ~131 and ~215 area) in `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`.
- Add the calibration subsection next to the existing concurrency section; keep the existing structure and cross-references.
- Add the measurement section to `docs/dev/fanout-validation-report.md` mirroring the audit F7 report layout.
- Re-grep for stale defaults and record the audit in the work item comment.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`
- `docs/dev/fanout-validation-report.md`
- `docs/dev/test-ceiling-validation.json` (linked artifact)

# Right-size `AUDIT_CHILD_SCREEN_TIMEOUT` and quarantine capped-screen verdicts

**Parent:** SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG (audit wall-clock reduction)
**Discovered-from:** WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B (ContextHub) · **RCA:** `docs/dev/audit-child-demotion-rca.md`

## Problem statement

Child Phase-1 AC screens run on a fixed `_CHILD_SCREEN_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT = 600` s budget (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` ~L631-642, env `AUDIT_CHILD_SCREEN_TIMEOUT`). On a loaded reference host that budget is **marginal, not generous**: in the 2026-10-21 ContextHub run, **5 of 11** child screens landed exactly on the cap (600.03–600.12 s) and 6 completed in 336–506 s. The capped screens then burn a further `verdict_reask` (2 more calls hit 600 s) and finally fall back to `partial` diagnostics.

Consequences beyond lost wall-clock (the parent epic's concern):

- **Tainted verdicts.** `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY calls=27 parse_ok=20 parse_failed=7 timeouts=7` — 26 % of calls produced no usable verdict, and 8 of 11 children were persisted as `Ready to close: No` on that tainted evidence.
- **Wrong lifecycle outcomes.** Those tainted 'No's were then persisted through `wl audit-set`, whose `revertToPlanComplete` side effect demoted all 11 `in_review` children (see the sibling bug item for that defect). Right-sizing the budget removes the main *source* of tainted child verdicts.
- **Selection bias.** Children whose FILE SCOPE is small (docs/XS items) complete comfortably; children with 6–7 ACs and wide manifests cap out, so the ones most likely to need judgement are the ones that lose it.

## Measured data (2026-10-21, ContextHub, 16-core host, load ~3)

| child screen | elapsed (s) |
|---|---:|
| F1 `WL-0MVFRR98A008MM19` | **600.12** (capped) |
| F2 `WL-0MVFRRAXD001E7AN` | 336.41 |
| F3 `WL-0MVFRRCP7007UWS7` | **600.11** (capped) |
| F5 `WL-0MVFRREMZ0085G7I` | **600.05** (capped) |
| F8 `WL-0MVFRRGGC001IQK1` | 506.12 |
| F4 `WL-0MVFRRKKN00544PQ` | 337.44 |
| F6 `WL-0MVFRRMX3003UPP3` | 258.12 |
| F7 `WL-0MVFRROLM002K98B` | 463.25 |
| F9 `WL-0MVFRRQ9W003KEFL` | **600.03** (capped) |
| F10 `WL-0MVFRRS2I000G93J` | **600.05** (capped) |
| F11 `WL-0MVFRRTY5001KTNH` | 394.36 |

Completed-screen distribution: min 258 s, median 389 s, max 506 s — i.e. the **unconstrained** p95 is already ≈506 s, leaving ~15 % headroom against a 600 s cap. Any host-load increase converts completions into timeouts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The child-screen budget is derived from measured data rather than a hard-coded constant: p95 of completed child screens across the recorded corpus, multiplied by a documented safety factor (proposal: ≥ 2× — this host's completed p95 is 506 s, implying ≈1,000–1,200 s), with the derivation recorded in a comment/docstring and the constant updated.
- The chosen value is validated against the corpus: re-running the measurement shows ≤ 5 % of child screens landing on the cap (currently 45 %), with the measurement command documented.
- A capped child screen is never reported as a plain `partial` indistinguishable from a model judgement: its evidence names the timeout and the phase, and the run's `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY` surfaces `child_screen_timeouts=N` so downstream consumers can quarantine it.
- The interaction with the parent-process budget is checked: raising the child-screen cap must not make the parent `--parent-timeout` (110 s + 600 s/child) the new starvation point; adjust that scaling formula in the same change if needed, and note the trade-off.
- FILE SCOPE and AC-count correlation is recorded (children capping out had 6–7 ACs and wide manifests) so a future manifest-width bound can be evaluated.
- `skill/audit/tests/` passes.

## Out of scope

Reducing the *number* or *cost* of child Phase 1 calls (parent epic AC5) and concurrency sizing (parent epic AC3) — this item only fixes the budget itself and the observability of a capped screen.
## Parent AC traceability

- **AC2 (parent)** — the derived child-screen budget is validated against the corpus using
  the measurement harness from parent AC1 (the sibling harness child), satisfying the
  "validated against the corpus ... measurement command documented" requirement.
- **AC4 (parent)** — capped screens are no longer indistinguishable `partial` fallbacks and
  are counted in `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY`, directly reducing the wasted-call share that
  parent AC4 measures.
- Out of scope for the parent epic's AC3 (concurrency ceiling) and AC5 (Phase 1 call
  count) — owned by sibling children.
data.title: Right-size the child-screen budget and stop treating capped screens as valid verdicts

# Audit performance measurement harness and committed baseline

**Parent:** SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG — Audits take too long: investigate and speed up

## Goal (user story)

As an operator or release producer, I want a committed, reproducible measurement of
audit LLM call timing, so I can verify that a performance change actually helped
instead of guessing.

## Problem statement

Every audit log on this host contains `Per-call timing:` lines, but no committed tool
parses them. The parent brief's baseline (1,637 instrumented calls, 140.8 h total,
62 % of call time in Phase 1, ~18 % wasted on timeouts and JSON re-asks) was produced
ad hoc and cannot be reproduced or regression-gated.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 (parent):** `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` is committed. It parses `Per-call timing:` lines from `~/.audit_debug/` (configurable root) and prints the per-context table with columns: context, calls, total, p50, p90, max, and count-at-budget. Running it on this host reproduces the parent brief's baseline figures within expected variance (documented tolerance).
- **AC1 (parent):** The harness is covered by a unit test using a small fixture corpus of synthetic debug logs — the test is written before the parser logic (TDD) and asserts each aggregate column including the count-at-budget buckets (600 s, 900 s, 1,800 s).
- **AC2 (parent):** `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` records the measured baseline (calls, total hours, per-context breakdown, Phase 1 share, wasted share) together with the reproduction command and a stated single-item audit wall-clock target of **≤ 10 minutes** on a healthy proxy with no concurrent audits, which becomes the regression gate.
- **AC2 (parent):** The baseline document names the gate explicitly and is referenced from `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.
- The harness is read-only: it never writes to `~/.audit_debug/`, `.worklog/`, or the audit runner.
- UK English throughout.
- **Parent AC1 traceability:** a script `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` parses `Per-call timing:` lines from `~/.audit_debug/` and prints the per-context table (calls, total, p50, p90, max, count-at-budget); running it on this host reproduces the baseline in this brief within expected variance; it is covered by a unit test with a fixture corpus.
- **Parent AC2 traceability:** the measured baseline (1,637 calls / 140.8h / 62% Phase 1 / 18% wasted) is committed to `docs/dev/` and a small-item audit wall-clock target of **≤ 10 minutes** (healthy proxy, no concurrent audits) is stated and used as the regression gate.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

1. Write `scripts/tests/test_measure_audit_performance.py` against a fixture corpus
   (5–8 synthetic logs spanning each context) — asserts table shape and aggregates.
2. Implement `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` with `--root`, `--context`,
   `--at-budget` CLI options and stable table output.
3. Run it on this host; record the output in `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md`
   with the mandated ≤ 10 min target and reproduction command.
4. Link the baseline doc from `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` — new harness
- `scripts/tests/test_measure_audit_performance.py` — new unit tests + fixture logs
- `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` — new baseline + target document
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — link to the baseline document

## Dependencies

None — this is the foundation slice; every other child depends on it.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the recorded `~/.audit_debug` corpus is representative (491 items,
  one host). The document records the host, date range and per-context counts so a
  different corpus is obviously different.
- **Risk:** debug logs may be pruned during the work; the fixture corpus makes the unit
  test independent of live logs while the baseline document pins the snapshot.
data.title: Audit performance measurement harness and baseline

# Size audit concurrency ceiling to real proxy slot capacity

**Parent:** SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG — Audits take too long: investigate and speed up

## Goal (user story)

As an implementation agent or release producer, I want the audit runner's parallel-call
ceiling to match the proxy's real slot capacity, so calls do not queue behind slots and
inflate their own timeout budget into avoidable 600 s / 1,800 s caps.

## Problem statement

`AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` defaults to 6 (`skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`) while
`GET /llama/local/status` reports `total_slots: 2`, `available_slots: 0`. Six concurrent
`pi` sessions queue behind two slots; queue wait is charged against each call's timeout,
inflating p90 and pushing calls onto their budget (96 calls at 600 s, 13 at 1,800 s).
Slot-status querying already exists (`skill/audit/scripts/scan.py`) but is only used for
the *child* ceiling.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC3 (parent):** The audit runner derives its parallel-call ceiling from live slot status (`available_slots` / `total_slots`) with a safe floor of 1, never exceeding reported capacity.
- **AC3 (parent):** When the slot query fails or times out, the runner falls back to the configured static ceiling (current behaviour preserved).
- **AC3 (parent):** An explicit `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` value remains authoritative — it is never silently overridden by slot discovery.
- **AC3 (parent):** Unit tests prove all three behaviours: 2-slot proxy ⇒ ceiling ≤ 2; failed query ⇒ configured fallback; explicit env var ⇒ that exact value.
- The ceiling derivation is logged once per run (slot status, derived ceiling, source) so the decision is observable in the audit log.
- Full `skill/audit/tests/` suite passes.
- **Parent AC3 traceability:** the audit runner derives its parallel-call ceiling from the live slot status (`available_slots` / `total_slots`) with a safe floor, never exceeding that capacity, falling back to the static ceiling when the query fails; unit tests prove 2-slot proxy ⇒ ceiling ≤ 2; failed query ⇒ configured fallback; explicit `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` remains authoritative.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

1. Write the failing concurrency tests first in
   `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py` (mock slot status).
2. Add a `_resolve_audit_ceiling()` helper in `audit_runner.py` that queries slot status
   (reusing the existing `scan.py` query), clamps by floor 1 and `total_slots`, and
   honours an explicit `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`.
3. Route every ceiling consumer through the helper (parent and child paths).
4. Log the derivation once per run; update the constant docstring in
   `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` to describe the derivation rather than a bare 6.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — ceiling resolution and consumers
- `skill/audit/scripts/scan.py` — existing slot-status query to reuse
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — ceiling default documentation
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py` — new tests
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — ceiling behaviour section

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the measurement harness + baseline child (SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG child 1):
  the change must be measured before/after with the committed harness.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (contention):** a slot-derived ceiling could still contend with interactive
  sessions. Mitigated by the floor of 1 and never exceeding `available_slots`.
- **Assumption:** `available_slots` is a trustworthy signal for admission; the fallback
  path keeps the runner functional when it is not.
- **Constraint:** do not raise timeouts to compensate — this change reduces queueing,
  not the budget.
data.title: Size audit concurrency ceiling to real proxy slot capacity

# Eliminate JSON-contract re-asks

**Parent:** SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG — Audits take too long: investigate and speed up

## Goal (user story)

As an implementation agent, I want a well-formed model response to be accepted on the
first call, so audit wall-clock is not spent re-asking — and the re-ask itself (p50
461 s, slower than the call it retries) is not billed twice.

## Problem statement

121 `verdict_reask` calls cost 18.7 h (13 % of all measured call time) and exist only
because the first response was not parseable JSON. `_reask_json_array_once` is the
fallback path; parse robustness is not hardened, so genuine-but-unusual formatting
(fenced blocks, prose prefix, trailing commas) triggers a full second call.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC4 (parent):** Parse robustness is hardened — a strict schema instruction is added to the prompt, tolerant extraction handles fenced ```json blocks and prose-prefixed JSON, and a single retry is attempted **only** on genuine failures (no parseable array found, or failed schema validation).
- **AC4 (parent):** A regression test proves a well-formed model response is never re-asked (the retry path is not invoked when the first response parses).
- **AC4 (parent):** Additional regression tests cover fenced blocks, prose-prefixed JSON, and trailing-comma tolerance — each accepted without a re-ask.
- **AC4 (parent):** A re-measurement on the same corpus shows `verdict_reask` at ≤ 2 % of all calls (currently ~7.4 %), recorded in the baseline document's successor report.
- Verdict semantics are unchanged: no response that would previously have been re-asked and then rejected may now be silently accepted with different semantics; the `met`/`unmet`/`partial`/`adjusted` vocabulary and the ready-to-close gate are frozen.
- Full `skill/audit/tests/` suite passes.
- **Parent AC4 traceability:** parse robustness is hardened (strict schema instruction, tolerant extraction, single retry only on genuine failures) and a regression test proves a well-formed model response is never re-asked; measured `verdict_reask` count drops to ≤ 2% of calls in a re-measurement on the same corpus.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

1. Write the failing tests first in
   `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_json_contract_reask.py`: well-formed ⇒ no re-ask;
   fenced ⇒ parsed; prose-prefixed ⇒ parsed; trailing comma ⇒ parsed; genuinely
   unparseable ⇒ exactly one re-ask.
2. Harden `_extract_json_array` (tolerant extraction) and add an explicit JSON-schema
   instruction to the Phase 1 prompt template.
3. Gate `_reask_json_array_once` on genuine failure only; count re-asks in the
   `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY`.
4. Re-run the measurement harness and record the re-ask share.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — prompt template, `_extract_json_array`,
  `_reask_json_array_once`, reliability summary
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_json_contract_reask.py` — new tests
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — JSON contract section
- `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` — re-measurement record

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the measurement harness + baseline child (child 1) — the ≤ 2 % claim must
  be measured with the committed harness.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (correctness):** tolerant parsing could accept malformed verdicts. Mitigated by
  schema validation after extraction and by keeping the retry for genuine failures.
- **Constraint:** verdict semantics are frozen (parent brief §Constraints).
data.title: Eliminate JSON-contract re-asks

# Fingerprint from item data only, v2 line

**Parent:** SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0 (Simplify audit freshness: invalidate only on this work item's own data change)

**User story:** As an audit operator, I want the audit content fingerprint computed from this work item's own data only, with zero git calls, so an unrelated commit — or even a change to a file this item touched — never invalidates a stored audit.

**Producer decision (2026-10-21, comment SA-C0MVIAGIQU003WW4P):** option (a) — the strict item-data-only formula (title + description, zero git calls) supersedes the per-touched-path formula from SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P. This is the core slice of the parent item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_compute_content_fingerprint` hashes a canonical JSON payload of **exactly** `{"schema": 2, "title_hash": <sha256(title)>, "description_hash": <sha256(description)>}` (`sort_keys=True`, then sha256 hex of the serialised payload). No `path_states`, no `key_files`, no comment-derived input (the Key Files section is part of the description and therefore already covered by `description_hash`).
2. The computation performs **zero git invocations**: it does not call `_resolve_touched_files`, `_compute_path_fingerprints` or any `git` subprocess, and is correspondingly fast (no repo probing) — asserted by a test that patches the git-executing helpers to raise.
3. `_compute_content_fingerprint` returns `None` (fail open → full re-audit) only when the work item cannot be fetched (`wl show` failure) or the payload cannot be built; a missing/garbage description still yields a deterministic hash.
4. `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX` becomes the **versioned** `"Audit content fingerprint (v2): "`; `_extract_content_fingerprint` returns a value only for `v2` lines and returns `None` for unversioned legacy lines, so legacy reports fall through to the existing time-gate floor (`AUDIT_FRESHNESS_BUFFER_SECONDS` + persist-write tolerance) with **no silent mass re-audit wave**. All three persist sites (~5714, ~5740, ~6158) emit the versioned line.
5. The now-unused `comments` parameter of `_compute_content_fingerprint` is removed and every call site updated: `_check_audit_freshness` (~2020), `_get_child_audit_verdict` (~6606), `_run_remediation_loop` (~10171), `_phase_fetch_and_cq` (~10357), `_reaudit_budget_exceeded_children` (~10786), `_phase_children` (~11516, ~11918). `cmd_check_freshness` (~2117/2120) keeps working and reports `hasFingerprint` from the versioned line.
6. **TDD, same commit:** the per-touched-path and comment-contribution invalidation tests are rewritten to assert the new rule *before* the behaviour change, and the change lands only when `skill/audit/tests` is green — the repo gate forbids a red commit, so code + test migration are one commit (`<WIP-id>: <summary>` recorded on this item).
7. Docstrings on `_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_check_audit_freshness`, `_extract_content_fingerprint` and `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX` describe the item-data-only, zero-git, versioned-line contract; no docstring still claims path/worktree/comment components.
8. Verdict semantics unchanged: `--force` still bypasses the gate; the freshness skip still returns the stored `rawOutput` verbatim (an explicit `Ready to close: No` is never masked).

## Minimal implementation

- Rewrite `_compute_content_fingerprint` in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` to the item-data-only payload; drop the `comments` parameter and its plumbing.
- Version the prefix constant and make `_extract_content_fingerprint` version-aware (v2 only; legacy → `None`).
- Migrate the affected tests in `test_audit_runner_freshness.py`, `test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py`, `test_no_breakage_chore.py`, `test_audit_runner_remediation.py` (literal-prefix assertions → the v2 constant).
- Keep `_resolve_touched_files` untouched (still used by the Phase-2 file-scope manifest at ~5257/~7964/~10897); dead-code removal is a separate item.

## Constraints

- Read-only: no test-suite execution or `pi` calls from the fingerprint path.
- Do not re-design the consumers (child reuse, read-only probe, ship `isAuditFresh`) — they must keep working against the simplified formula, not be extended.
- Documented trade-off (accepted): a stored audit may reference code that later changed, including files this item touched. The audit verdict remains the record for the item's own data.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_compute_content_fingerprint`, `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`, `_extract_content_fingerprint`, `_check_audit_freshness`, persist sites, call sites
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` — rule migration
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py` — probe expectations
- `skill/audit/tests/test_no_breakage_chore.py` — literal prefix assertions
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_remediation.py` — literal prefix assertion
data.title: Fingerprint from item data only, v2 line

# Remove dead fingerprint git/comment machinery

**Parent:** SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0 (Simplify audit freshness: invalidate only on this work item's own data change)

**User story:** As a maintainer, I want the git/comment machinery that only the old fingerprint needed removed, so the freshness path is smaller and no future change can quietly resurrect a repo-state component.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_compute_path_fingerprints` (~2336) is deleted once it has no callers; the tests whose only subject was that helper (`test_compute_path_fingerprints_*`, `TestTouchedFileResolution` ~311-344 in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py`) are removed with a note in the item ledger comment (`_FakeGitRepo` usage reviewed — keep only what other tests still need).
2. `_fetch_item_comments` (~2163) is deleted if it has no remaining callers (it existed to make the fingerprint's comment contribution deterministic); if any caller remains, it must be named in the item comment with the reason it stays.
3. `_resolve_touched_files` (~2213) and `_compute_path_fingerprints`'s sibling helpers are **retained** where still used by the Phase-2 file-scope manifest (~5257, ~7964, ~10897) and their tests stay green; `_resolve_audited_head` (~2852) is retained for green-run attestation.
4. Test scaffolding that patched the removed helpers is cleaned up: the `_deterministic_fingerprint` autouse fixture and `_DEFAULT_STATES` / `_DEFAULT_TOUCHED` constants and the `states=` parameter of `_fingerprinted_raw` in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_children.py`. Fixtures that remain must express the item-data-only contract, not a pinned path state.
5. Grep evidence recorded in an item comment: no reference to the removed symbols remains in `skill/audit/**`, `skill/ship/**` or `scripts/**` (excluding the docs owned by the documentation item), and `python3 -m compileall` / import of the audit runner succeeds.
6. `/skill:test` changed-scope run is green after the deletion.

## Minimal implementation

- Confirm each deletion with a grep, then run the changed-scope suite via `/skill:test`.

## Constraints

- A helper is only removed when a grep proves it has no production caller.

# Update freshness-gate documentation

**Parent:** SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0 (Simplify audit freshness: invalidate only on this work item's own data change)

**User story:** As an agent or operator reading the audit docs, I want the documented freshness rule to match the shipped code — item data only, versioned line, legacy fallback — so I do not design around a per-touched-file gate that no longer exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` freshness-gate section (~248-318, plus the re-audit-coordination bullets ~579-594 and the child-reuse mentions ~699/816) is rewritten to the new contract: the content fingerprint covers the work item's **own data only** (title + description, which contains the ACs and Key Files), with **zero git calls**; unrelated commits, working-tree churn, changes to files the item touched, comments, and lifecycle-field changes do **not** invalidate; description/title/AC/Key-Files changes do.
2. The same file documents the **versioned line** (`Audit content fingerprint (v2): <sha256hex>`), the legacy/unversioned fallback to the time-gate floor, and the resulting one-time re-audit consequence for legacy in-review items whose `updatedAt` moved after their audit — including its interaction with the pre-flight full-suite cache gate (a re-audit of a legacy item can block on the cache gate, the exact failure seen on SA-0MSN04X2S006ONH0).
